title: The 200 day average rule that beat holding QQQ since 2000 lost to just holding SPY and the Dow
author: person-person12
selftext:
I posted the QQQ version of this elsewhere and the fair pushback was whether it holds up on anything else, which is the right question, because a rule that only works on the ticker it got famous on is mostly a story about that ticker. So I ran the exact same rules in [Agenticks](https://www.agenticks.ca/?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=post&utm_campaign=autopilot&utm_content=ai_trading) on SPY, DIA and IWM, daily candles from 2000 to March 2026 (IWM starts May 2000, QQQ is the earlier run to the end of 2025), $10k start, $0.50 commission and 3 cents a share of slippage on every buy and sell.

The rules:

* buy when it closes above its 200 day simple average
* sell when it closes back below
* both fill at the next open

Against holding the same ticker from the first day the 200 day average existed:

* **QQQ**: +782% against +707% holding, worst drop 24% against 77%
* **IWM**: +121% against +89% holding
* **SPY**: +300% against +348% holding, worst drop 22% against 56%
* **DIA**: +85% against +321% holding, worst drop 36% against 54%

So it beat holding on the two that crashed hardest and lost on the two that didnt. On the Dow it was a mess, 112 trades at a 24% win rate, and **$4,046 of costs** came out of a gross gain of about $12,600, so a third of what it made went to getting in and out on every whipsaw around the line.

The drawdown side held on every one of them. Even on DIA, where it gave up most of the return, the worst drop was a third smaller than holding.

comments.author: TheGaseousCharade
comments.body: The DIA result is brutal. Going from $10k to just $18.5k while buy and hold gets over $42k really shows how expensive whipsaws can become. I use Moon for shorter market wagers and this makes me appreciate that a signal can be useful for limiting drawdowns without actually creating superior returns. The fact it worked on QQQ doesn't make it universal.

replies.author: person-person12
replies.body: Yea thats exactly it. On QQQ the rule got you out of 2000 and 2008, and on the Dow there was never a crash deep enough to pay for **112 round trips at a 24% win rate**. It still cut the worst drop from about 54% to 36% tbh, which is worth something to anyone who would have panic sold holding through the first one.
